extracted.intended_audience: PhD students nearing completion (potential applicants) and institutional nominating partners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for applicants and nominating partners on who the Schmidt Science Fellows program seeks, the selection criteria (qualities/characteristics) for candidates, and specific eligibility dates/requirements for the 2027 cohort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target disciplines and interdisciplinary commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: We are seeking brilliant minds in natural sciences, math, engineering, and computing with a commitment to interdisciplinary science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should come from natural sciences, engineering, mathematics, or computing and demonstrate commitment to interdisciplinary approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual Achievement
rubrics_metrics.description: Sustained evidence of academic scholarship in science and technology, demonstrating an exceptional intellectual ability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for a track record of high-quality scholarship and achievements that indicate exceptional intellectual capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curiosity
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrated intellectual exploration, creativity, and openness to new ideas, methods, or technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence might include pursuit of novel questions, creative approaches, or adoption/development of new methods or technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary Pivot
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear readiness and motivation to move beyond the PhD discipline, supported by evidence of interdisciplinary thinking, learning agility, and comfort with scientific risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should show motivation and preparedness to pivot into a new discipline area, with examples of interdisciplinary thinking or willingness to take intellectual risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence of effective collaboration across diverse teams, including behaviors that build trust, cohesion, and shared purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for demonstrated teamwork, ability to work in diverse groups, and concrete examples of contributing to team cohesion and shared goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character and Leadership Potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Early indicators of future scientific leadership appropriate to career stage, such as initiative, perseverance, humility, and positive influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess for behaviors and examples that show emerging leadership qualities (initiative, resilience, humility, influence) suitable for early-career scientists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific and Societal Impact and Awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrated understanding of the role of both fundamental and applied sciences in advancing knowledge and society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should show awareness of how science connects to societal challenges and the potential impact of research both fundamentally and practically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Be nominated by your PhD awarding institution, which must be one of our nominating partner organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only candidates nominated by listed partner institutions are eligible; applicants should consult the Nominating Partner Organizations list and contact nominations@schmidtsciencefellows.org if their institution/contact is not listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible PhD fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Be studying for a PhD in natural sciences (astronomy, biology, chemistry, physics, and earth sciences), engineering, mathematics, or computing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be in one of the enumerated fields; social sciences, political science, and economics are generally outside the eligible fields (see ineligibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: PhD conferral date window
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete all the requirements for the conferral of your PhD, including a successful defense, between May 1, 2026 and June 30, 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must finish all PhD requirements within the specified dates to be eligible for the 2027 cohort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical ineligibility — clinical-track and veterinary programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Please note that the following applicants are typically not eligible for this program: Individuals on clinical track MD‑PhD or veterinary‑PhD programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These program tracks are normally excluded, but the page notes individual circumstances may vary and invites contact to discuss specific cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical ineligibility — social/political science and economics pivots
rubrics_metrics.description: Please note that the following applicants are typically not eligible for this program: PhD students in social and political science or economics. Applications proposing a pivot into social or political science, or economics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pivoting into social/political science or economics from eligible STEM fields is generally not acceptable; contact the program if uncertain about particular situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application support and contact guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: If your institution or contact information is not listed, please contact nominations@schmidtsciencefellows.org. Please refer to our FAQ for other queries about eligibility or the application process. If you still have further questions, please contact us at apply@schmidtsciencefellows.org.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural support: check partner list first, consult the FAQ, and use provided email contacts for nomination or application queries. The program allows case-by-case discussions for uncertain eligibility.
